topic: Mahito could reshape almost every soul except Yuji's, because Sukuna lives in it
title: Why Mahito Could Never Touch Yuji's Soul
description: Mahito's Idle Transfiguration worked on nearly everyone, so why not Yuji? Here's my read on the Sukuna detail behind it. Do you agree?
comment: Was Mahito scared of Yuji, or just curious about him? Pick one.

lines.text: Mahito could rewrite almost anyone's soul. Yuji was the one he couldn't touch.

shot.fallback: pale patchwork curse reaching toward a teenage boy

lines.text: And I think that's exactly why he obsessed over him.

shot.fallback: curse staring at a pink haired boy

lines.text: Idle Transfiguration works by touch. Mahito reshapes the soul, and the body follows.

shot.fallback: curse spirit with hand on a glowing soul

lines.text: In episode 11, he does it to Junpei, a kid with no protection at all.

shot.fallback: tragic schoolboy twisted into a monster

lines.text: People say Yuji just has a tougher soul. But toughness isn't the rule. Shape is.

shot.fallback: boy facing a curse in a dark corridor

lines.text: Here's the detail most fans forget.

shot.fallback: glowing soul with a shadow inside

lines.text: Sukuna lives inside Yuji, and Mahito can't reshape a soul the King of Curses already occupies.

shot.fallback: giant demon king looming inside a boy's soul

lines.text: That's my read, anyway, and it fits every scene they share.

shot.fallback: curse and boy facing off in a ruined street

lines.text: Gojo and Sukuna were the only others on that short list.

shot.fallback: white haired sorcerer and king of curses

lines.text: So the curse that treated souls like clay found the one he could never mold.
Because Mahito could rewrite almost anyone's soul...

shot.fallback: pale curse with a cruel smile

self_check.hook: line 1 names Mahito and a contrarian claim
